cd /Users/vitaliy/Documents/GitHub/local-whisper
git add -A
git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
Replace ffmpeg mic capture: it was dropping ~10% of every recording

ffmpeg's avfoundation *input device* hands over roughly 90% of what it
captures. Measured with a fixed output duration: a `-t 20` run took 21.11s
of wall clock, ffmpeg reported a 20.00s timeline, and the file held 18.04s
of PCM. Every 1-second chunk it wrote came out 0.885-0.917s long, so the
loss is spread evenly -- about 100ms missing from every second. That
swallows short words whole, and because whisper is generative it papers
over the gaps with fluent invented text: the transcript reads better than
the truth while missing words, which is what made it hard to notice.

None of these changed it: -thread_queue_size, -drop_late_frames false,
-use_wallclock_as_timestamps, -capture_raw_data, -audio_device_index,
:0 vs :default, dropping the segment muxer, or dropping the resampler
(native 48kHz loses the same). It is inside the indev.

tools/lw-record.swift taps AVAudioEngine's input node instead and loses
nothing -- chunks come out at exactly 1.000000s. init.lua builds it on load
when missing or stale, so there is still no install step. ffmpeg remains
correct and unchanged for segment concat and for all format conversion in
tools/transcribe.sh; only the microphone moved.

The recorder doubles as the warmup probe. Previously a throwaway
`ffmpeg -f null` open was followed by a second open for the real recording,
so the device was opened twice per dictation and everything spoken during
the probe went to /dev/null. lw-record prints READY once its engine is
actually running and has been recording since before that line, so the
lead-in is kept.

Also:

- Restore splitAtSilence(). Segments over 55s are transcribed by independent
  whisper calls, so a fixed-index cut lands mid-word and the word is mangled
  across the seam -- a real transcript showed seg 1 ending "...чтобы меня
  передавали." and seg 2 opening "давали по звучанию." It was written once,
  deleted in the dead-feature cleanup, and is now covered by tests.

- Mixed-language (surzhyk) handling on both paths. Whisper decodes each
  window into one language and normalises the rest into it. The initial
  prompt is the only lever, and it is a writing sample rather than an
  instruction. ~/.local-whisper/prompt is seeded with a ru/uk/en sample;
  the local path adds --carry-initial-prompt so the anchor survives past
  whisper's first 30s window, and transcribeViaAPI now sends the same text
  as `prompt` plus temperature=0 -- it previously sent no prompt at all, so
  the LAN model normalised the mix exactly as whisper-cli did.

- Fix a chunk-directory race. stopRecording() dropped the task handle while
  the recorder was still flushing, so a fast re-press cleared CHUNK_DIR out
  from under it and the old tail was spliced onto the next transcript. The
  handle now lives until the process exits, tryWarmup() kills a slow
  predecessor first, and each task's callbacks ignore output once superseded.

- Health check: every recording logs captured-vs-wall-clock seconds, so a
  future capture regression is visible instead of silent. It is parsed in
  the streaming callback because hs.task leaves the termination callback's
  stdout empty whenever a streaming callback exists.

- setup.sh no longer prompts for AUDIO_DEVICE. It patched a constant that no
  longer exists, so the prompt was a no-op; capture follows the macOS default
  input device now.

Tests: 85 checks pass. New `capture` and `split` guards were each verified to
fail on the bug they claim to catch by mutating the current file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
MSG
